public_rationale: Published verification experiments complicate the suggestion that LLMs cannot check their answers. They do not settle the stronger claim that a proper world model guarantees avoidance of this particular error. Neither the required model definition nor a controlled test of the presidential-tenure example was located. Treating probabilistic generation itself as proof of the causal claim would not be justified.
limitations: The cited experiments concern different tasks and models.
A literal interpretation excluding every form of self-checking would invite a different assessment from the ordinary reliability reading.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Any system that could properly leverage widely available data into a proper world model could fact-check itself and would not make this error (showing two presidents in office at once), whereas LLMs leave everything to statistical chance.
conditions: system that could properly leverage widely available data into a proper world model

statement.excerpt: Again any system that could properly leverage the widely available data into a proper world model could fact check itself, and would not make this error. LLMs leave everything to statistical chance.
statement.document_title: LLMs are not like you and me—and never will be.

from_speaker: properly leverage the widely available data into a proper world model
LLMs leave everything to statistical chance
our_interpretation: The particular error is a depiction of incompatible, overlapping US presidential tenures.
The ordinary reading contrasts reliable factual consistency checking with generation that does not guarantee such consistency.
Statistical chance is not interpreted as uniform random guessing.
A proper world model must be defined independently of whether the system gives the correct answer; otherwise the proposed explanation becomes circular.
The scope is systems and mechanisms relevant to the August 2025 claim.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evidence establishes that an independently specified representation of presidential tenure, when used for checking, prevents the error, and implementation evidence establishes the asserted absence of reliable factual constraints in the relevant LLM systems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A relevant LLM demonstrably enforces factual tenure constraints, contradicting the universal contrast, or a system meeting independently specified world-model criteria still makes the error despite using that representation.

evidence.explanation: The experiments show that language-model verification can improve factual answers. They qualify a reading that excludes all self-checking, but do not establish guaranteed factual constraints or test presidential overlap errors.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independently specified world-model criterion and reproducible tenure tests that isolate representation, checking, and rendering, together with implementation evidence about factual constraints.
